speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. As I examine your newborn, I notice you are presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; how long have these symptoms been occurring since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. Given the bilious vomiting, history of feeding intolerance, and older sibling with pyloric stenosis, have you noticed any abdominal distension or passage of stool in the past six hours?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The abdominal X-ray demonstrates a 'double bubble' sign, which is indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Brother had pyloric stenosis. Social history: NA

speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal atresia with Down syndrome.

The combination of bilious vomiting in a newborn with epicanthal folds, a single transverse palmar crease, and a holosystolic murmur strongly suggests intestinal obstruction, likely duodenal atresia, rather than gastroenteritis. Please confirm the Abdominal X-Ray results to look for the classic "double bubble" sign.
